definition: Simulates Antimatter Beam Ships operating for a day.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where antimatter traps monitoring, pion propulsion redundancy, or magnetic nozzles maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Antimatter Beam Ships Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Antimatter Beam Ships: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Antimatter Beam Ships — starships driven by beamed antimatter annihilation.

Phase 1 — Prove (antimatter traps): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (pion propulsion): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (magnetic nozzles): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (fuel logistics): beam hull as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and deep-space-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
